chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I had two bags of musk, one wet and the other dry. I started with the wet one and sold it, then took the dry one to sell it. I found that I was not given for the dry one the price that matched it, nor did they add to me beyond the price of the wet one. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it suitable for me to call it out (announce its quality)? He said: 'No, unless you inform them.' So I called it out, then I informed them, and he said: 'There is no harm with it if you inform them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling dry musk at the same price as wet musk without disclosure?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of selling mixed-quality goods by distinguishing between inherent uncertainty (*gharar*) and mere difference in value. The key condition for validity is the seller's active disclosure (*ta'lim*) of the quality disparity to the buyer, ensuring that the transaction is based on informed consent rather than deception. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency in commercial contracts to prevent disputes arising from hidden defects or varying standards.
